missions.title: Lunar radiation campaign (lunar orbit), built on the Mars structure
missions.record_note: The cycle-by-cycle run reports for this campaign were lost with a laptop. This debrief is rebuilt from what survives: the campaign's published summaries, two published figures with their data, and the stored model records from August 2026. The stored model records hold more than numbers: each relationship carries the cycle it was admitted in, the admission statistic, the prediction registered for it, and what was learned. So for this mission you can say which hypotheses were tried, which cycle admitted or refuted each one, and with what numbers. What you cannot give is the reasoning text of each cycle. If someone asks for that, say the run reports are not available for this mission.
scope_limits: Lunar orbit only. No lunar surface measurements.
record_limits: No run reports: cycle numbers, admission statistics and registered predictions come from the stored model records; the reasoning text of each cycle is lost.

opening.spoken: The lunar radiation campaign, which took what was learned at Mars and pointed it at the Moon.

short_version.spoken:
In August 2026 the system took the structure it had learned at Mars and pointed it at the Moon. It did not start from nothing: it carried over which drivers matter, and it wrote down in advance one thing it expected to flip. At Mars the atmosphere soaks up solar particle events and surface dose goes down. The Moon has no atmosphere, so the prediction was that the same events would push dose up. That is what the lunar data showed. Same Sun, opposite signs, ordered by shielding.

The data is dose in lunar orbit from the CRaTER instrument on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, seventeen years of it.

The headline finding is about warnings. In the first half of 2024 the system found three episodes where dose at the Moon rose by large factors while Earth's official solar-event catalog had nothing. Each was missed in a different way, and each was confirmed by an independent spacecraft in lunar orbit.

What is open: the Earth's magnetotail seems to affect lunar dose in the opposite direction to the textbook, and that is unexplained. And nothing here comes from the surface.

What is needed: access to the one surface dataset that exists, and monitoring near the Moon instead of relying on Earth-side alerts.

what_happened.spoken: The lunar model was seeded on August 10, 2026, from the Mars structure. The proton-event relationship was registered with its sign reversed against Mars, with the stated reason: no atmospheric column, so prompt particle enhancement dominates. The model was split by where the Moon is: in the solar wind, or inside Earth's magnetotail. Four versions followed. The first ran seven loop cycles on dose in physical units. The second, the same evening, re-based the model on the logarithm of dose and ran ten cycles. The third split the hours into storm and quiet and ran eight. A fourth, a week later on August 17, re-seeded the whole structure and ran two cycles. Across the four, the same drivers kept being admitted: proton flux, the recovery pattern after events, depth inside the magnetotail, and solar activity. The stored records also hold three counts and measurements that were not hypothesis tests. Counting the same way across seventeen years, sixty quiet-day radiation bursts were found, and forty-four of them fall in 2023 to 2025; the year 2012, loud by Earth standards, has none. The instrument's three detector pairs behaved coherently in each of the three missed episodes, which separates soft events from penetrating ones and rules out an instrument fault. At its peak on June 8, 2024, the shallow channel read about eleven hundred times its baseline. These are stated from the published summary and the figures.

rely_on.spoken: particle events hit the Moon at full strength, and they can be large when Earth's catalog is silent.

do_not_rely_on.spoken: Earth-side alerts alone for decisions near the Moon. The campaign's own summary is that anyone operating near the Moon needs lunar-vicinity monitoring.
geomagnetic indices as controls in the solar wind; they learned weight where they were expected to abstain, and why is not settled.

new.spoken: the steady background from galactic cosmic rays is a construction problem, because lunar soil is available as shielding. The acute problem is warning time, because surface work has to stop and people have to reach shelter.

day_zero.spoken:
A lunar base starts with no surface data. What the system would bring on day zero is this.

What carries over: the structure. Which drivers to watch, the split between solar wind and magnetotail, the split between storm and quiet hours, and the expectation that particle events raise dose.

What is unknown: every relationship at the surface. Each would start at its seed value with no certainty, and would have to be learned from the base's own instruments.

What to measure first: a dosimeter at the surface, read hourly. Monitoring near the Moon that does not depend on Earth's catalog. Coverage of magnetotail passes during storms, which the orbital record barely has.

certainty_statement.spoken: Certainty is set aside for this mission. The first three versions show certainty collapsing on every relationship, as at Mars. The fourth version, under a new scale, shows several relationships at or near the ceiling of certainty. Those values are not reported, because a correct scale is not supposed to let certainty reach its ceiling, and the rule that sets the scale is being worked out. Say what was found and what confirmed it.

preregistered.question: Did the two 2024 solar-wind stream interfaces found at Mars reach the Moon, at the meetings predicted by corotation?
preregistered.rule: Test A: Earth's solar wind (OMNI) shows a speed step of at least eighty kilometres per second with a doubling of field or pressure within a day, inside two days of the predicted meeting. Test B: the Moon's cosmic-ray rate (CRaTER) dips to the bottom tenth of a null distribution within minus one to plus three days. 'Same structure seen at Mars and at the Moon' may be said only where A fires and B dips at the same meeting, with both base rates printed beside it.
predictions: PA1: the February structure reached Earth (M1 or M2 fires)
PA2: the June structure reached Earth (M3 or M4 fires)
PB1: every meeting where A fires shows a dip
PB2: dips are a few percent, half to five

numbers.m3_baseline_confound: late-May solar particle event tail in the baseline days

misses: PA1 failed: the February structure was not seen at Earth's longitude at either meeting; the Earth-blind reading stands for it.
PB2 failed at M3: the dip was nine percent, larger than the registered half-to-five percent range, with the baseline sitting in a solar-particle-event tail that the registered flag did not catch.

cycles.spoken: On October eighteenth, under a rule written before any 2024 solar-wind or cosmic-ray byte was read, Nervous Machine asked whether the two stream interfaces found at Mars in 2024 had also reached the Moon. The February one was not seen at Earth's longitude at either predicted meeting. The June one met the rule at one meeting: Earth's solar wind stepped up on June fourth, and the Moon's cosmic-ray rate dipped at the same time, in the bottom two percent of the null distribution. The base rates are thirty six percent for the solar-wind test and ten percent for the dip, so a random meeting passes both about four percent of the time. That makes it suggestive, not strong. One confound travels with it: the baseline days sat in the tail of a late-May particle event, which inflates the dip. A second cycle with a better particle flag is specified and open to anyone with the public data.

findings.spoken: Earth's alerts are not enough at the Moon. Between January 10 and July 7, 2024, three dose episodes at the Moon are missing from the official solar proton event catalog. The first, March 15 to 18, was missed by threshold. Dose at the Moon stayed at least four times normal for four days, peaking at about forty times normal on March 16. The proton measure the catalog watches only grazed its alert line and fell back, so nothing was recorded. The ARTEMIS spacecraft in lunar orbit saw it directly, at about three times background. The second, May 9, was missed by latency. Dose rose at the Moon a full day before the catalog opened an event. The first electrons arrived ahead of the protons the catalog watches. ARTEMIS read about two hundred times background while Earth-side protons read under one particle flux unit. The third, June 8 to 10, was missed by curation. These were the highest dose days of the whole window, around one hundred and forty-eight thousand micrograys per day on June 8, against a quiet level near one hundred and twenty. It was declared a strong radiation storm in real time, and yet the catalog file skips from May 13 to September 9. ARTEMIS ions read about one thousand eight hundred times background.

findings.spoken: Storm hours and quiet hours need separate weights. In the fifth loop cycle a flux-linear form confirmed its first prediction, that the weight would sit at its ceiling, and failed its second: the fit gain was about four percent against a registered expectation of at least fifty. The measured ceiling was about eighteen-fold. The answer was a third version of the model with storm and quiet hours split, in which the same drivers were re-admitted.

findings.spoken: Two geomagnetic indices, ap and kp, were registered as controls in the solar wind: with no mechanism there, they were expected to learn nothing. They learned weight anyway. The kp index came out at about minus zero point three nine in the first version, and the control was re-registered and re-tested in the second and third versions, each time with the expectation that its weight would stay under zero point one zero. It did not: about minus zero point one six, then about minus zero point one three. The abstention prediction failed three times. What that means is still open: either the indices carry something real that the model has no name for, or the learning rule lets a driver with no mechanism absorb structure it should refuse.

standing.basis: registered as controls expected to abstain in the solar wind; learned weight in all three versions
